newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates in the doldrums after quiet week.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates in the doldrums after quiet week.

text.p: Crude tanker rates across most sectors remained in the doldrums on Friday, as a week-long lull in fixing activity took its toll.
Brokers attributed the lack of activity to the week of oil functions in London as well as seasonal factors such as refinery turnarounds in the Far East.
"It's been fairly quiet, but it should pick next week with IP week out of the way," said one broker.
Rates for VLCCs out of the Middle East bound for Japan had slipped to below W57.5 by the end of the week -- the first time since October -- against last week's average of W65.

"This is probably best explained by over-tonnage situation and the anticipated reduced activity due to the forthcoming refinery shutdowns in Korea and Japan," shipping brokers Gibson said in their weekly report.
The UK/Cont market was the one sector to see a slight rise in rates due to the usual end of month scramble for tonnage, the effects of which were expected to carry on into next week.

"The 20th of the month is the usual time when many charterers are given their stem confirmations for the next month and thus the succeeding week is generally the busiest of the month, that is of course next week," brokers Galbraith's said.

The Caribbean experienced a dismal start to the week, with the U.S. President's Day holiday slashing trade, but had picked up by the end of the week. Rates for 70,000 tonners on up U.S. coast were up to W120 on Friday from the previous W110-115, but were regarded as fairly low for the season.

The Med and West Africa markets trundled along, but brokers expected action to pick-up next week. Rates for 130,000 tonne cross-Med trips were pegged at W80-85 and at W90 for West Africa/United States trips.
